results.title: Inter-department football tourney concludes at KU
results.description: Srinagar, Aug 13: The Inter-Department Football Tournament, organised by Directorate of Physical Education and Sports, University of Kashmir (KU) concluded on Thursday at the University’s Ground “B”, marking the culmination of a vibrant student-centric sporting activity. The tournament witnessed an overwhelming response, with over 19 teams representing various departments and satellite campuses of the University. The tournament was organised as part of the annual sports calendar of the Directorate of Physical Education and Sports, formulated earlier this year. The grand finale witnessed an exciting match between the Department of Management Studies and the Department of Computer Sciences. In a closely contested match, the Department of Management Studies emerged victorious with a 1–0 win. Mukaram scored the decisive goal in the 20th minute, helping his team clinch the championship trophy. The concluding ceremony was presided over by Director, Physical Education and Sports, Prof. Raies Qadri. Addressing the gathering, Prof. Raies Qadri congratulated both teams for exhibiting a great performance and precision throughout the tournament. He assured the players of every possible support from the Directorate in terms of coaching, training and sports equipment. He further informed that outstanding performers from the tournament would be shortlisted for participation in the forthcoming Inter-College Football Tournament, providing them an opportunity to represent Varsity’s Post Graduate team. Head, Department of Management Studies, Prof. Mushtaq Siddiqi, appreciated the Directorate for organising such student-centric sporting initiatives and said that regular sports activities play an important role in the holistic development of students. Prof. Raies Qadri and Prof. Mushtaq Siddiqi distributed trophies and medals among the winning and runner-up teams. The tournament was coordinated by Assistant Director, Dr. Basharat Ali, while the proceedings of the concluding ceremony were conducted by Football Coach, Sajid Yousuf Dar.

results.title: Vance says low oil prices are top US goal in Iran conflict
results.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. — Vice President JD Vance said Thursday that the top US priority in the Iran war was keeping oil and gasoline prices low for Americans, with preventing Tehran from acquiring a nuclear weapon ranking second. The remarks constrasted with President Donald Trump's repeated framing of the fight: that entering the war had the sole objective of preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon, even if that meant short-term economic sacrifices for Americans. Vance's comments also underscored the growing reality that the war now centers on control of the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has forced to the top of the negotiating agenda. "I know that oil is down today and it's way down from the highs in the early days of the conflict," Vance said on Fox News. "That's goal number one -- keep oil and gas cheap for Americans all over our country." "And then obviously goal number two is ensure that Iran never gets a nuclear weapon," he added. The vice president has been among the members of the administration most skeptical of the offensive launched against Iran in late February. His latest remarks, however, appear to confirm the more cautious approach now favored by the US president, which involves maintaining strong economic pressure on Iran while a military standoff in the Strait of Hormuz persists. "Sometimes we're focused on the energy piece of it because we want Americans to be able to afford the price of oil and gas. Sometimes we're obviously focused on the military... on the nuclear program," Vance also said. Vance added that Trump was "at the height of his authority with a lot of tools -- diplomatic, military and economic." The decision to focus on economic pressure comes as the diplomatic path appears blocked, with both Washington and Tehran sticking to their conditions for reopening the strait. Regarding his military options, US media report that Trump must contend with rapid depletion of stocks of certain missiles and drones.

results.title: Chong Wei highlights 3 key discipline issues
results.description: Chong Wei highlights 3 key discipline issues ammar_hakim@as... Fri, 14 Aug 2026 - 10:46 Lee Chong Wei has once again highlighted the three disciplinary issues plaguing the national shuttlers: Refusing the stay in the hostel, going out during international tournaments and skipping training. The Badminton Association of Malaysia (BAM) performance committee chairman confirmed he said he met the national coaches earlier this week to discuss how to address these issues. “I met the coaches to discuss these issues. The coaches must look into this, they know better. Besides, I’m not in BAM daily. But, if the coaches need any help, they can call me. I can help,” said Lee at the trophy unveiling ceremony of the Lee Chong Wei Cup recently. “These disciplinary issues will take time to resolve, we cannot fix it within a few days. We must address it step by step. Speaking to our coaches, we realize our players discipline are bad. It’s better than before, but will take time to fix. “It’s like coronavirus, it has infected other shuttlers from just a few,” he added. Lee had previously raised concerns on the shuttlers’ discipline, especially to those violating the rules by not staying at the Academy Badminton Malaysia. The rules dictate that only married players are allowed to live outside. This even prompted senior shuttler Aaron Chia to tell his junior counterparts to get married if they do not wish to stay at the national badminton academy hostel.
